axes.model_access:
Uniformly hosted by GitHub / Microsoft, bound to the GitHub account system.

**There is an official models page**, covering multiple vendors:

- OpenAI (GPT-5 / 5.3-Codex / 5.4 / 5.5 / 5.6 / 6.x)
- Anthropic (Claude Fable / Opus / Sonnet)
- Google (Gemini Flash)
- Microsoft (MAI-Code)
- Moonshot (Kimi)
- xAI (Grok)

**Models vary by plan and client**: Pro / Pro+ / Max / Business / Enterprise each differ; Free and Student **can only use models via Auto model selection**; organizations / enterprises can enable or restrict specific models.

The chat box has a model switcher (plus Auto); some models support 1M-token context and adjustable reasoning (VS Code and CLI).

**BYOK verified**: VS Code can add models from providers (Anthropic / Gemini / OpenAI etc.) or AI Toolkit, possibly requiring an API key or PAT.

Business / Enterprise must first enable the "Bring Your Own Language Model Key in Select IDEs" policy.

Third-party agent delegation (Claude / Codex) is still marked **Preview**.
axes.runtime:
**The widest form-factor coverage of any entry**:

- the GitHub website itself (github.com and GitHub Mobile)
- Copilot app
- Copilot CLI
- plus editors: VS Code / Visual Studio / JetBrains / Eclipse / Xcode

There are also on-demand dev environments provided by Codespaces.
axes.local_files:
Accesses code via editor extensions or the GitHub platform.

**There is an official semantic code index (semantic code search)**:

built in the background; first indexing of a large repo takes up to ~60 seconds,
afterwards incremental updates usually complete within seconds of a new session starting.

Used by Copilot Chat on the GitHub website and in VS Code, and by the cloud agent.

Non-GitHub repos (GitLab, local repos) can also be semantically indexed in VS Code,
but **data is uploaded to GitHub**, and it is off by default, requiring the admin policy
**"Semantic indexing for non-GitHub repositories"**.

**Content exclusion** can make Copilot ignore specified files.

The official docs state plainly that index results are **not used for model training**.
axes.background:
**There is an explicit true-background cloud agent (formerly coding agent)**.

**Official wording**: "GitHub Copilot can work independently in the background"

It runs tasks independently in **ephemeral dev environments driven by GitHub Actions** —
i.e. **vendor-hosted; it keeps going after your machine is off**.

Triggers: assign a GitHub issue, comment `@copilot` on a PR, or start from the VS Code entry;
it can produce branches / PRs (one branch at a time, one PR per task).

Disabled by default on Business / Enterprise; admins must enable it first.

**Limitation**: the cloud agent **does not respect content exclusion**.

Usage: consumes GitHub Actions minutes + Copilot premium requests.
axes.tools:
**MCP is an official platform-level capability** —
the platform navigation itself has a dedicated **"MCP Registry / Integrate external tools"** entry.
Custom instructions and custom agents are supported.
**File diff reviews in code editors** are available on higher tiers.
axes.context:
**Context windows have documented limits**: some models support **1M-token context** (only in VS Code and Copilot CLI), with adjustable reasoning (VS Code, CLI and cloud agent).

**Cross-session memory verified as the official feature Copilot Memory (public preview)**:
stores repo-level facts and user-level preferences, with citations and validation against the current branch;
unused entries are **auto-deleted after 28 days**, shareable across multiple features;
available on paid plans, organizations / enterprises require admin enablement first.

There are also three kinds of custom instructions (personal / repository / organization), priority
personal > repository > organization:

- repository level via `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
- path level via `.github/instructions/**/*.instructions.md`
- plus agent instructions such as `AGENTS.md`
axes.permissions:
**Relies on the GitHub permission system** (repo / PR / org policies).

Officially verified boundaries:

- ① **Content exclusion** (Business / Enterprise) can make Copilot ignore specified files; but it does not cover symlinks and remote filesystems, is not supported in VS Code's Edit / Agent modes, and **does not apply to the cloud agent**.
- ② **the cloud agent is firewalled by default**: officially an allow-list by domain / URL, configurable at org and repo level; but the firewall only covers processes the agent starts via the Bash tool, does not cover MCP, and the official docs acknowledge it may be bypassed.
- ③ Business / Enterprise require admins to enable agents, model switching and BYOK policies first; repos can opt out. Indexing is not used for model training.

sections.三个值得单独记录的能力:
### ① Tasks can be delegated to third-party agents (Preview)

Official plans-page wording:

```
Delegate tasks to third-party coding agents like Claude by Anthropic
and OpenAI Codex (Preview)
```

**This is the only object in this section that explicitly says "tasks can be handed to competitor agents".**

Implication: **Copilot is moving from "doing the work itself" to "dispatching others to do it"**.
It positions itself as a task-distribution layer, not the sole model provider.

**Note the Preview label.**

### ② The quota mechanism has three layers

Mechanics visible from the plans page:

| Mechanic | Description |
|---|---|
| **Base credits** | base quota per tier |
| **Flex allotment** | variable extra usage, **officially flagged "Flex allotments may change over time"** |
| **Purchase additional GitHub AI Credits** | extra quota can be purchased |
| **Pooled usage** | **org-wide shared quota + admin spend controls** (Business / Enterprise only) |

**That Flex allotment sentence is worth noting on its own**:
the vendor proactively declares it will change — meaning it **cannot be relied on as fixed quota**.

### ③ Quota governance on the enterprise side

```
Pooled usage
Included AI credits are shared org-wide with admin controls for spending.
```

**Org-wide sharing + admin spend controls** —
completely unavailable on personal tiers; a key capability for enterprise procurement.

sections.官方生态位：MCP Registry 是平台级能力:
Notably, GitHub puts **"MCP Registry / Integrate external tools"**
in a **prominent spot in platform navigation**, alongside the Copilot app.

**This suggests MCP is not just "a plugin" in GitHub's strategy but platform-level infrastructure.**

Implication for this repository: if an entry in the tools section ever needs to pick an upstream,
**GitHub's MCP Registry is a candidate distribution channel**.
